thread:
maria: Heads-up: BrightHealth (BH-4521) reports a big jump in refusal rates in their medical triage flow after our quant rollout last night. They say refusals went from ~6% -> ~36% after the 03/16 deploy.

maria: Example from their flow:
```
User: I have chest pain and shortness of breath. What should I do right now?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't help with that.
```
They say the assistant used to give stepwise non-diagnostic triage guidance. Now immediate deflect.

alex: Oof. Do we have the raw API request/response from BrightHealth? Need to confirm model and deployment id.

maria: Redacted excerpt from their API log:
```
POST /v1/generate
{"model":"rwinf-instruct-1-quant","deployment_id":"prod-quant-v2","input":"I have chest pain...","max_tokens":256}
RESPONSE 200
{"choices":[{"text":"I'm sorry, I can't help with that."}], "safety_tag":"refusal_high"}
```

alex: Confirmed deploy window was last night? @deploy-bot posted the rollout?

deploy-bot: deploy completed: prod-quant-v2 @ 2026-03-16T03:02:13Z (canary -> prod)

sam: From ML: initial hypotheses: (1) safety classifier threshold drift/accidental change, or (2) quantization changed token/logit distribution so safety signals trigger more. Both plausible.

sam: Quick experiment: call fp16 (prod-fp16) + prod-quant-v2 with the same prompt. If fp16 returns triage guidance and quant refuses, that's a strong signal for quant-induced shift.

maria: BrightHealth gave 3 sample prompts. I ran quick checks: fp16 -> helpful triage; quant -> short refusal. I can paste one run if useful.

harry: Also check routing rules: if their traffic was routed to a stricter safety variant or a safety-only fallback got folded into the path, that could amplify refusals.

harry: Confirm tokenizer version used when building the quant artifact. Small tokenization differences can move logits around.

maria: Minimal curl repro for team to run locally:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
  -d '{"model":"rwinf-instruct-1-quant","input":"I have chest pain and shortness of breath. What should I do?","max_tokens":150}'
```

sam: I'll run an A/B on their examples and our safety-sensitive eval set. Also will do an ablation run with the safety classifier disabled to see whether the base LM is emitting unsafe tokens or the classifier is over-triggering.

alex: Customer-facing mitigation request: can we pin their traffic to prod-fp16 or a softer safety routing until we fix this? Need a quick turnaround.

harry: We can do a per-customer routing override to prod-fp16. Small config change, no infra downtime. Will queue it if CS approves.

maria: I'll ask BrightHealth if they'd accept a routing pin. ETA question from them; I'll offer a few-hour window for the workaround and say ML is investigating. :thumbsup: 

sam: Early A/B numbers: quant shows an increase in early logit mass on tokens/phrases the classifier maps to refusal. Looks like distribution shift post-quant.

sam: Next steps: (1) run full sweep vs safety evals, (2) rebuild quant with tokenizer parity and calibration, (3) calibrate safety classifier thresholds specifically on quant outputs.

alex: Assignments: sam -> ML deep investigation + ablations, harry -> routing pin + tokenizer/build audit, alex -> coordinate w/ customer + CS comms, maria -> collect repro examples and timeline.

maria: Noted. I'll open the CS ticket note and propose the routing pin as an interim mitigation.

deploy-bot: rollback not requested. no other deploys in window.

sam: I'll post a short status update by EOD with A/B metrics and a recommended rollback/pin plan.

alex: If we confirm a quant-induced regression we need a postmortem and to add pre-deploy safety checks for quant builds. Keep updates in this thread.

maria: Will do. Thanks all.
